title: Fit a disc lock through a vent hole in a parked scooter's front brake disc and press its plunger home
instruction: Lock the scooter's front brake disc with the disc lock.
context: Scooter and motorcycle riders fit a disc lock at almost every stop. Its 5.5 mm pin only goes home through one of the disc's vent holes: slid on blind, the pin stops on the steel, the lock is not shut and falls off, so one hand has to hold the lock square on the 4 mm disc with the pin over a 9 mm hole while the other presses the plunger.
setup: Front end of a 50 cc scooter facing +y, left side to the robot, all fixed except the wheel. Wheel centre at x=40.0, y=0, 21.8 cm above the surface; it turns about the x axis. Tyre 3.50-10, rubber, 43.4 cm across, 8.9 cm wide; alloy 10-inch rim with 5 spokes. Steel brake disc 22.0 cm across, 0.4 cm thick, its mid-plane 7.2 cm outboard of the tyre's centre plane (x=32.8), with nine 0.9 cm vent holes on a 19.4 cm circle, 40 degrees apart; at the start two of them sit 20 degrees below and 20 degrees above the disc's front point (y=+9.7 cm, at wheel-centre height). Black fork legs 3.4 cm across (centres 10.0 cm either side of the wheel's centre plane) rise 25 degrees back from the axle to a crown 42 cm up the leg, with a 4.4 cm steering stem above; black caliper 5.5 x 4.2 x 4.2 cm over the disc's rear upper part (centred 140 degrees round from the front, 9.5 cm out); red fender (12 cm wide) over the tyre from 35 to 150 degrees. Disc lock (stapler-class, Kryptonite Keeper 5-S2 class): yellow zinc-alloy C body 3.8 x 7.9 x 3.2 cm, 0.54 kg, 0.7 cm jaw gap, slot 3.0 cm deep, steel 0.55 cm pin on a sprung plunger (20 g, 1.0 cm travel, 4 N at full press) with a 1.6 cm black cap standing 1.0 cm proud, caught when pressed home. It lies flat on the surface at x=27.0, y=19.0 cm (pin axis 1.6 cm up), its slot facing the wheel (-y), the pin along +x. Distractors (loose, ignored by scoring): sunglasses 14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, plastic and glass, 0.03 kg at (16, -20) cm, yaw 0.4 rad; paper coffee cup 8.5 cm across, 11.7 cm tall, 0.25 kg at (62, 30) cm; cotton rag 26 x 23 x 2 cm, 0.04 kg at (20, 38) cm, yaw 0.3 rad. Coordinates from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left; surface height 74.75 cm.
scoring: Locked: the plunger caught by the lock's catch (pressed at least 9.5 of its 10 mm, cap within 0.5 mm of flush) and still at least 9 mm in, with the pin's axis within 4.5 mm of a vent hole's centre where it crosses the disc (the pin through that hole). 1.0: locked, both grippers at least 3 cm from the lock, the lock still (under 1 cm/s and 0.1 rad/s) and the wheel still (under 0.02 rad/s), all for 2 s in a row. 0.5: locked at the end but a gripper is within 3 cm of the lock, or it has not been still for 2 s. 0: anything else (the pin stopped on the steel, the cap standing proud, the lock off the disc or on the floor, or caught with no vent hole round the pin). If the caught lock ever comes within 3 mm of the brake caliper or the fork leg (the wheel turned with the lock on), the trial scores 0 whatever follows.
reset_notes: Unlock the disc lock with its key, set it back on its tape marks with the plunger out, and turn the wheel back to its start mark (paint dot on the tyre against a tape mark on the fender). Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Full-size rigid scooter front end: the wheel turns on a fixed axle against an elasto-plastic friction drive (1.0 N m to start it, 0.8 N m turning; an estimate) standing in for bearing, pad and floor drag; the body past the fork crown is left out. The disc's vent holes are real 12-sided collider holes. The lock is a rigid C body with a straight sprung plunger (400 N/m, estimated) and a joint-lock catch for its stapler action and key. Uniform friction, no force sensing. Distractors: SimReady.
